destinations.name: Lisbon
destinations.tagline: Mild winter sun and hilltop views.

details.why: The summer crowds are gone and the days are still mild. On 11 November the city celebrates São Martinho, and roasted chestnut carts fill the street corners.

go.name: Miradouro da Senhora do Monte
go.map: Miradouro da Senhora do Monte, Lisbon
go.note: One of the highest viewpoints in the city. Arrive half an hour before sunset.

go.name: Alfama before 10am
go.note: Wander the old lanes before the tour groups arrive.

go.name: Belém
go.note: Jerónimos Monastery, then custard tarts at Pastéis de Belém.

go.name: LX Factory
go.note: A former industrial complex full of shops, bars and the Ler Devagar bookshop.

skip.name: Tram 28 at midday
skip.note: Packed, slow and a favourite with pickpockets.
skip.instead: Ride it before 9am, or walk the route.

skip.name: The Santa Justa Lift queue
skip.note: A long wait for a very short ride.
skip.instead: Walk to the top from Largo do Carmo.

skip.name: Restaurants with touts on Rua Augusta
skip.instead: Eat at a local tasca in Graça or Campo de Ourique.

dishes.name: Bacalhau à Brás
dishes.note: Shredded salt cod scrambled with straw potatoes, egg and onion. The dish to start with.

dishes.name: Amêijoas à Bulhão Pato
dishes.note: Clams cooked with garlic, olive oil, lemon and coriander. Mop up the sauce with bread.

dishes.name: Peixinhos da horta
dishes.note: Green beans in a light batter, fried until crisp. The name means "little fish from the garden".

dishes.name: Pastel de nata
dishes.note: Flaky pastry filled with caramelised custard, best eaten warm with cinnamon.

places.name: Ramiro
places.note: A busy seafood hall on Avenida Almirante Reis, known for its clams. Expect a queue at peak times.

places.name: Laurentina, O Rei do Bacalhau
places.map: Laurentina O Rei do Bacalhau, Lisbon
places.note: A long-standing restaurant on Avenida Conde Valbom devoted to salt cod.

places.name: Manteigaria
places.note: Custard tarts baked in front of you, with several branches across the city.

history.name: The Age of Discoveries
history.note: Vasco da Gama sailed for India from Belém in 1497. The riches of the spice trade paid for the Jerónimos Monastery, begun a few years later.

history.name: The 1755 earthquake
history.note: On 1 November 1755 an earthquake, a tsunami and days of fire destroyed most of the city. The straight streets of the Baixa are the rebuild that followed.

history.name: Alfama
history.note: The oldest quarter, with a street plan that goes back to Moorish times. It came through 1755 better than the lower town, which is why its lanes still twist.

history.name: 25 April 1974
history.note: The Carnation Revolution ended almost half a century of dictatorship, nearly without bloodshed. The red suspension bridge over the Tagus is named after the date.

nightlife.name: Bairro Alto
nightlife.note: Hilly lanes packed with small bars, cheap drinks and crowds that spill into the street. The liveliest area after dark.

nightlife.name: Pink Street, Cais do Sodré
nightlife.note: A former red-light street turned bar strip. Pensão Amor is the best-known stop, and MusicBox has live music and DJs.

nightlife.name: Fado at Tasca do Chico
nightlife.note: A small, informal fado bar with two branches. Bairro Alto is livelier, Alfama more intimate. Go early, it fills fast.

nightlife.name: Lux Frágil
nightlife.note: The city's best-known club, in a former warehouse by the river with a rooftop bar. The door is selective, so dress the part.

destinations.name: Kotor
destinations.tagline: A dramatic bay, quiet lanes and off-season prices.
destinations.go: The Ladder of Kotor at dawn
destinations.skip: The Old Town on cruise ship days

details.why: The summer crowds have gone and prices drop, but the bay is at its most dramatic. Pack a raincoat: November is one of Kotor's wettest months, so save the climbs for a dry morning.

go.name: The Ladder of Kotor at dawn
go.note: A free switchback trail above town with sweeping views of the bay. Start early and wear proper shoes.

go.name: Perast
go.note: A tiny baroque town about 20 minutes along the bay, facing the island church of Our Lady of the Rocks.

go.name: A konoba in the Old Town
go.note: Warm up in a traditional tavern with Njeguši ham, local cheese and a glass of Vranac red.

go.name: The Old Town after 5pm
go.note: Once the day-trippers leave, the squares, churches and famous cats have the place back.

skip.name: The Old Town on cruise ship days
skip.note: Day-trippers can pack the narrow lanes from late morning.
skip.instead: Check the port's cruise schedule and explore early or after 5pm.

skip.name: The €15 fortress climb on a wet day
skip.note: The limestone steps get slippery and the view can vanish into cloud.
skip.instead: Wait for a dry morning. From 1 December the climb is free.

skip.name: Driving into the Old Town area
skip.note: Parking is scarce and expensive, and clamping is common.
skip.instead: Park outside the centre and walk in.

dishes.name: Mussels na buzaru
dishes.note: Boka Bay mussels cooked in white wine, garlic, olive oil and parsley.

dishes.name: Crni rižot
dishes.note: Black risotto coloured with cuttlefish ink, a legacy of Venetian rule.

dishes.name: Njeguški pršut and cheese
dishes.note: Smoky dry-cured ham and sheep's cheese from the mountain village of Njeguši, above the bay.

dishes.name: Ispod sača
dishes.note: Lamb or veal slow-roasted under an iron dome covered in embers. Hearty, and right for a wet November day.

places.name: Konoba Scala Santa
places.note: A family-run konoba on Trg od Salate in the Old Town, known for black risotto and fish stew.

places.name: Stari Mlini
places.note: A restaurant in a centuries-old mill by the water at Ljuta, along the bay. Fish, mussels and a clay-pot dish of the day.

places.name: Marenda Grill House
places.note: Grilled meat a short walk outside the Old Town walls. Check opening hours before you go, as winter schedules vary.

history.name: A walled port
history.note: Kotor has been a trading port since Roman times. St Tryphon's Cathedral, at the heart of the Old Town, was consecrated in 1166.

history.name: Venice, 1420 to 1797
history.note: Almost four centuries of Venetian rule gave the town its walls, palaces and the winged lions still carved above its gates.

history.name: The 1979 earthquake
history.note: A major earthquake badly damaged the Old Town in April 1979. The same year UNESCO listed Kotor as a World Heritage Site, and the restoration took years.

nightlife.name: November is quiet
nightlife.note: Kotor's nightlife is a summer affair. Off season, evenings mean a long dinner and a drink in the Old Town rather than clubs, and some bars close for a few weeks.

nightlife.name: Old Winery Wine Bar
nightlife.note: Local Vranac by the glass with a plate of ham and cheese, and jazz in the background.

nightlife.name: Pub Old Town
nightlife.note: A lively pub with an international crowd, open all year.

nightlife.name: Maximus
nightlife.note: The big club built into the walls by the Sea Gate. It peaks in July and August, and in winter it opens only for events, so check first.

details.why: On 27 November Ljubljana switches on its festive lights and its December celebrations begin. Come earlier in the month for quiet streets and lower prices, or late for the lights. Mornings are often foggy, so save the views for the afternoon.

go.name: Prešeren Square, 27 November
go.note: The festive lights switch on at 5pm, opening the city's December celebrations.

go.name: The Central Market
go.note: Fresh produce, cheese and local snacks by the river. Go in the morning, Monday to Saturday.

go.name: Ljubljana Castle
go.note: Walk up for views over the red rooftops. Best in the afternoon, once the morning fog lifts.

go.name: Metelkova
go.note: Former army barracks turned into a graffiti-covered alternative arts quarter.

skip.name: The castle funicular
skip.note: You pay for a ride that lasts about a minute.
skip.instead: Walk up from the old town in around 15 minutes.

skip.name: Driving into the centre
skip.note: The old town is largely car-free and parking is expensive.
skip.instead: Use a park-and-ride on the edge of the city and take the bus in.

skip.name: Lake Bled as a rushed half day
skip.note: November days are short, and a quick trip means more time on the bus than at the lake.
skip.instead: Give it a full day, or save it for another trip.

dishes.name: Štruklji
dishes.note: Rolled dough dumplings with fillings such as cottage cheese, walnut or apple, served sweet or savoury.

dishes.name: Kranjska klobasa
dishes.note: Smoked Carniolan pork sausage with garlic and pepper, served with mustard and horseradish.

dishes.name: Jota
dishes.note: A thick winter stew of beans, sauerkraut and potato, often with pork. Made for November.

dishes.name: Prekmurska gibanica
dishes.note: A layered cake of poppy seed, walnut, apple and cottage cheese.

places.name: Klobasarna
places.note: A small counter beside the cathedral that serves Carniolan sausage and little else. Quick, cheap and good.

places.name: Moji štruklji
places.note: A štruklji specialist with around a dozen fillings.

places.name: Gostilna na Gradu
places.note: Regional Slovenian dishes up at the castle, at higher prices. Book ahead.

history.name: Roman Emona
history.note: The Romans built the town of Emona here about two thousand years ago. Stretches of its wall still stand south of the centre.

history.name: The 1895 earthquake
history.note: A strong earthquake damaged much of the city. The rebuild brought the Art Nouveau facades you see around Prešeren Square.

history.name: Plečnik's city
history.note: Between the wars the architect Jože Plečnik reshaped Ljubljana: the Triple Bridge, the Central Market and the riverside embankments are his. UNESCO listed his work here in 2021.

history.name: A young capital
history.note: Slovenia declared independence from Yugoslavia in 1991, making Ljubljana a national capital.

nightlife.name: The riverside
nightlife.note: Bars and terraces line both banks of the Ljubljanica. Tozd, on Gallusovo nabrežje, is an easy first stop. In November, how lively it gets depends on the weather.

nightlife.name: Dvorni Bar
nightlife.note: A wine bar beside Congress Square with a long list of Slovenian wines.

nightlife.name: Nebotičnik
nightlife.note: The café and bar at the top of a 1933 skyscraper, with views to the castle. Best at sunset.

nightlife.name: Metelkova
nightlife.note: Clubs and live music in a former army barracks. Each space runs its own nights, so check what is on. It can feel empty when little is happening.

destinations.name: Marrakech
destinations.tagline: Warm days, cool nights and a film festival.
destinations.skip: Arriving at Majorelle without a ticket

details.why: The summer heat is gone: days reach around 22°C and evenings turn cool, so bring a layer. From 20 to 28 November the city hosts the 23rd Marrakech International Film Festival, and the public can watch films with a free e-pass for over-18s.

go.name: Ben Youssef Madrasa
go.note: A 16th-century Koranic school with a carved cedar and tiled courtyard. Open daily from 9am, 50 dirhams. Arrive at opening for the courtyard to yourself.

go.name: Jardin Majorelle, first slot
go.note: The cobalt-blue garden restored by Yves Saint Laurent. Book the earliest timed slot online, before the tour groups.

go.name: Le Jardin Secret
go.note: A restored riad garden in the middle of the medina. Climb the tower for views over the rooftops.

go.name: Jemaa el-Fna at dusk
go.note: Watch the square fill with food stalls, musicians and storytellers from a rooftop café, then go down and walk through it.

skip.name: Arriving at Majorelle without a ticket
skip.note: Tickets are sold online only and there is no ticket window at the gate.
skip.instead: Book on the official site, tickets.jardinmajorelle.com, a day or two ahead.

skip.name: Following a self-appointed guide in the souks
skip.note: Offers to show you the way usually end at a cousin's shop or a demand for money.
skip.instead: Use an offline map and say a polite no, or book a licensed guide through your riad.

skip.name: Airport taxi touts
skip.note: Drivers in arrivals often quote several times the fair price to the medina.
skip.instead: Use the official taxi counter in arrivals. In town, ask for the meter: "compteur, s'il vous plaît".

dishes.name: Tanjia
dishes.note: Marrakech's own dish: beef or lamb with preserved lemon and spices, slow-cooked for hours in a clay urn.

dishes.name: Tagine
dishes.note: Stewed meat or vegetables cooked under a cone-shaped lid. Try chicken with preserved lemon and olives.

dishes.name: Harira
dishes.note: A soup of tomato, lentils and chickpeas, often eaten with dates. Cheap, filling and right for a cool evening.

dishes.name: Msemen
dishes.note: Square, flaky griddle bread, eaten at breakfast with honey or soft cheese.

places.name: Chez Lamine Hadj Mustapha
places.note: In the lane of mechoui stalls by Jemaa el-Fna. Slow-roasted lamb sold by weight, and tanjia. Go at lunchtime.

places.name: Nomad
places.note: Modern Moroccan food on a rooftop above the spice square, Rahba Kedima. Book for sunset.

places.name: Al Fassia
places.note: A long-standing restaurant in Guéliz, run by women, known for classic Moroccan dishes. Book ahead.

history.name: An Almoravid capital
history.note: The Almoravid dynasty founded Marrakech around 1070 as the capital of an empire that stretched into Spain. The city gave Morocco its name.

history.name: The Koutoubia
history.note: The minaret of the Koutoubia Mosque went up under the Almohads in the 12th century. Its design influenced the Giralda in Seville.

history.name: The Saadian age
history.note: In the late 16th century Sultan Ahmad al-Mansur built the El Badi Palace and the Saadian Tombs. The tombs were sealed off and only rediscovered in 1917.

history.name: Majorelle and YSL
history.note: The painter Jacques Majorelle laid out his garden from the 1920s. Yves Saint Laurent and Pierre Bergé bought and saved it in 1980.

nightlife.name: How it works
nightlife.note: Alcohol is served in licensed bars, hotels and restaurants rather than in the souks. Hivernage, outside the medina walls, is where most of the late-night places are.

nightlife.name: Kabana
nightlife.note: A rooftop bar facing the Koutoubia minaret. Best at sunset.

nightlife.name: Le Salama
nightlife.note: A restaurant and rooftop bar a few minutes from Jemaa el-Fna, one of the few in the medina with a full bar.

nightlife.name: Comptoir Darna
nightlife.note: Dinner with music and dancers in Hivernage, turning into a lounge later in the night. Book a table.

destinations.name: Kyoto
destinations.tagline: Ginkgo gold and the first red maples.
destinations.skip: The Arashiyama bamboo grove at midday

details.why: Autumn colour is running late in 2026. The forecast puts Kyoto's yellow ginkgo at its best around 27 November and the red maples around 11 December, so the last week of November gives you gold trees and the first reds. Days are crisp and mostly dry, and nights get cold.

go.name: Fushimi Inari at dawn
go.note: Thousands of orange torii gates climbing the mountain. Open day and night and free. Start before 7am and keep climbing past the first viewpoint, where most people turn back.

go.name: Kiyomizu-dera at opening
go.note: The wooden stage over the valley opens at 6am. Go then, and walk down through Sannenzaka before the shops open.

go.name: The Philosopher's Path
go.note: A canal-side walk of about two kilometres from Nanzen-ji to Ginkaku-ji. Do it in the morning, and stop at Eikan-dō for maples.

go.name: Nishiki Market
go.note: A narrow covered market known as Kyoto's kitchen. Graze on pickles, tofu and skewers, but eat at the stall where you buy.

skip.name: The Arashiyama bamboo grove at midday
skip.note: The path is short and, by late morning, shoulder to shoulder.
skip.instead: Go by 7.30am, or walk on to the quieter Adashino Nenbutsu-ji, which has its own small bamboo path.

skip.name: Walking into Gion's private lanes
skip.note: Signs on the side lanes ban entry and photography, with fines of up to ¥10,000. Chasing geiko and maiko for photos is not welcome anywhere.
skip.instead: Stay on Hanamikoji, which is a public street, and the Shirakawa canal, and ask before taking anyone's picture.

skip.name: Bus 100 or 206 at peak times
skip.note: The main sightseeing buses are packed and slow in autumn.
skip.instead: Take the subway and walk, or at weekends the EX100 and EX101 sightseeing express buses (¥500) from Kyoto Station.

dishes.name: Yudōfu
dishes.note: Soft tofu simmered in kelp broth with a dipping sauce. A Buddhist temple dish, and made for a cold day.

dishes.name: Nishin soba
dishes.note: Buckwheat noodles in hot broth topped with sweet braised herring. A Kyoto classic.

dishes.name: Obanzai
dishes.note: Kyoto home cooking: small seasonal side dishes of vegetables, tofu and fish, often laid out on the counter to pick from.

dishes.name: Matcha sweets
dishes.note: Green tea in everything, from soft-serve to wagashi. Try it with a bowl of whisked matcha.

places.name: Okutan Nanzenji
places.note: A yudōfu restaurant by Nanzen-ji temple that has served the dish for centuries. Set menus only, in a garden setting.

places.name: Matsuba
places.note: The restaurant credited with creating nishin soba, by the Minamiza theatre in Gion.

places.name: Kagizen Yoshifusa
places.note: An old Gion sweet shop known for kuzukiri, cool arrowroot noodles dipped in black sugar syrup.

history.name: Heian-kyō, 794
history.note: The emperor moved the capital here in 794, and Kyoto stayed the imperial seat for over a thousand years, until the move to Tokyo after 1868.

history.name: The Ōnin War
history.note: From 1467 to 1477 rival clans fought through the streets and burned much of the city. Many of the temples you see were rebuilt after it.

history.name: Spared in 1945
history.note: Kyoto was on the shortlist of targets for the atomic bomb. The US Secretary of War, Henry Stimson, had it removed, and the city escaped heavy bombing.

history.name: A World Heritage city
history.note: In 1994 UNESCO listed seventeen temples, shrines and a castle as the Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto.

nightlife.name: Kyoto goes to bed early
nightlife.note: Temples close around 5pm and many restaurants stop serving by 9pm. The night is for a long dinner and a drink, not big clubs.

nightlife.name: Pontochō
nightlife.note: A lantern-lit alley along the Kamo River packed with restaurants and small bars. Check prices before you sit down.

nightlife.name: Bar K6
nightlife.note: A well-known whisky and cocktail bar on Kiyamachi, near Nijō.

nightlife.name: Club Metro
nightlife.note: A long-running club inside Jingū-Marutamachi station, with DJs and live nights. Check the schedule.

details.why: November is late spring: warm days, longer evenings and jacaranda trees in purple bloom across the city. On Saturday 14 November La Noche de los Museos opens hundreds of museums and cultural spaces for free, from 7pm to 2am. Bring an umbrella, as spring showers are common.

go.name: The jacarandas
go.map: Parque Tres de Febrero, Buenos Aires
go.note: Walk the Palermo parks and Plaza San Martín while the trees are in flower. The bloom lasts a few weeks.

go.name: Recoleta Cemetery
go.map: Cementerio de la Recoleta, Buenos Aires
go.note: A city of marble mausoleums, including Eva Perón's family tomb. Foreign visitors pay an entry fee, by card only. Go early.

go.name: San Telmo on a Sunday
go.map: Feria de San Telmo, Buenos Aires
go.note: The antiques and crafts fair fills Calle Defensa, with tango in Plaza Dorrego. Then lunch at the San Telmo market.

go.name: Teatro Colón
go.note: One of the world's great opera houses, opened in 1908. Take the guided tour, or better, book a performance.

skip.name: Changing money on Calle Florida
skip.note: Street changers offer no protection against fake notes or short counts.
skip.instead: Pay with a foreign Visa or Mastercard. These now get the tourist exchange rate. Always choose to be charged in pesos.

skip.name: La Boca beyond Caminito
skip.note: The painted street is fine by day, but the surrounding blocks are not a place to wander, especially after dark.
skip.instead: Go in daylight, stay on the main streets and take a taxi or app ride in and out.

skip.name: The big tango dinner show
skip.note: Expensive, staged and aimed at tour groups.
skip.instead: Watch the real thing at a milonga, such as La Catedral, where locals dance late into the night.

dishes.name: Asado
dishes.note: Beef grilled slowly over wood or charcoal. Order bife de chorizo (sirloin) or ojo de bife (ribeye).

dishes.name: Provoleta
dishes.note: A thick disc of provolone grilled until crisp outside and melting inside, with oregano.

dishes.name: Empanadas
dishes.note: Baked pastries filled with beef, chicken or ham and cheese. Cheap, everywhere and good.

dishes.name: Medialunas and dulce de leche
dishes.note: Small sweet croissants for breakfast, and the caramel spread that goes in almost every dessert.

places.name: Don Julio
places.note: A celebrated parrilla on a Palermo corner. Book well ahead, or expect a long wait for a table.

places.name: El Cuartito
places.note: A pizzeria open since 1934, walls covered in sporting photos. Order a slice of fugazzeta, the onion and cheese pizza.

places.name: Café Tortoni
places.note: The city's most famous café, open since 1858 on Avenida de Mayo. Go for the room and a coffee, not a meal.

history.name: Founded twice
history.note: Pedro de Mendoza founded a settlement here in 1536, but it was abandoned. Juan de Garay founded the city again in 1580.

history.name: May 1810
history.note: The May Revolution in the square now called Plaza de Mayo began Argentina's road to independence, declared in 1816.

history.name: The immigrant boom
history.note: Between about 1880 and 1930 millions of Europeans arrived, many from Italy and Spain. The grand avenues, Teatro Colón and the accent all come from that era.

history.name: The Mothers of Plaza de Mayo
history.note: From 1977 mothers of people disappeared under the military dictatorship marched in front of the presidential palace. They still walk there on Thursday afternoons.

nightlife.name: Late, then later
nightlife.note: Dinner rarely starts before 9.30pm, bars fill after midnight and clubs get going around 2am.

nightlife.name: Florería Atlántico
nightlife.note: A cocktail bar hidden in the basement behind a flower shop in Retiro.

nightlife.name: La Catedral
nightlife.note: A milonga in a former warehouse in Almagro, relaxed and a little bohemian. Beginners welcome, with classes early in the evening.

nightlife.name: Niceto Club
nightlife.note: A Palermo venue for live bands and club nights. Check what's on.
